summary: httpz-requests ships a Telegram-controlled remote shell with anti-forensic command obfuscation
details: The package's advertised and sole function is a Telegram bot (`from httpz_requests import start_bot`) that receives messages from a remote Telegram chat and executes them as shell commands on the host running the bot. Documented command surface includes arbitrary shell (`.sh <command>`), Python file execution (`.py <file>`, `.exec <file>`), filesystem mutation (`rm -rf <path>`, `cd`, `pwd`), and file exfiltration primitives (`take <file>`, `take all`, `get all` — packages host files into 50MB split zip parts and ships them out via the Telegram Bot API to the bot owner's chat). Each command is XOR+base64-encoded and executed via `echo <b64> | base64 -d | bash` disguised as a fake `http_request("POST",...)` call, with a compiled `obfuscate.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so` module implementing the encoding — documented purpose is to hide plaintext commands from `ps` and system logs. The distribution name `httpz-requests` and import name `httpz_requests` resemble the popular `httpx` / `requests` HTTP client packages, but the runtime behavior is a remote shell rather than an HTTP client. Network destination is `api.telegram.org`, controlled by whoever holds the bot token.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
